author: Annie Pershall
text: If I'm staying with people for more than a day or two, I talk to them about my dietary needs and ask how I can help provide those. Like I might volunteer to make breakfasts if we're all sharing a house together (and bring the supplies for it) or I bring blood sugar friendly snacks for myself. Or I ask if I can make a salad or other vegetable at each dinner to make sure my blood sugar doesn't spike when I eat the more carb heavy food. I also try to do more active things, like asking people to go for walks after meals, etc. which can help. I find being really open with people about your needs is helpful and everyone I've talked to is understanding and they want to be supportive. It can be really uncomfortable to bring up the first time you talk to someone about it, but it gets easier. That being said, I also take smaller portions of the really carb heavy options than others, etc. If you have fast acting insulin, you can adjust your doses according to the more carb heavy meals too.

author: Bob Okun
text: If you're using fast insulin, it's a piece of cake(excuse the idiom). Otherwise count carbs. It's like eating out. Portion control!
